title: Introduce rotating credential factory and pullstream-iterable UX
author: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Motivation: Several customers building long-lived streaming integrations reported edge cases around short-lived credentials (KMS-backed tokens, mTLS rotated certs) and complex consumer ergonomics for pull-based streaming.

This PR implements a small, focused surface change in the TypeScript SDK to make credential rotation explicit but low-friction, and to provide a pullstream-friendly async-iterable facade that keeps parity with the existing event-emitter push API. The goal is to: (1) surface a minimal rotating credential factory API that SDKs and platform components can implement; (2) provide an ergonomic async-iterable PullStream that resumes transparently across transient auth refresh and reconnects; (3) keep the default behavior backward compatible while enabling an opt-in ergonomic mode; (4) bump the SDK to v3.1.0 to release the ergonomics improvements.

Key points and constraints: This is intentionally conservative: no change to wire protocol, no server-side contract changes. The credential factory is pluggable and optional; the previous static token pattern remains supported. The PullStream adapter does not change message framing or streaming semantics, it only adapts to underlying reconnects and credential swaps.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement RotatingCredentialFactory with abortable refresh and leases
- [x] Add PullStreamIterable wrapper (async iterable) with resume semantics
- [x] Add comprehensive unit/integration tests simulating token expiry and reconnects
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes
- [x] Package bump and changelog entry

What changed (summary):
- New public API: RotatingCredentialFactory (interface) and RotatingCredentials (type) in src/auth/rotatingCredentialFactory.ts. A default implementation RotatingCredentialCache is provided which issues refresh callbacks and exposes a getCurrent() + onChange() hook.
- New public API: PullStreamIterable in src/stream/pullstreamIterable.ts that returns an AsyncIterableIterator of framed messages and automatically attempts to recover from transient network/auth failures using the provided credential factory.
- Small helper: reconnect backoff config was extracted to src/stream/backoff.ts and shared between the PullStream and existing push-streams.
- Tests added under tests/streaming and tests/auth to cover expiry, mid-stream rotation, and recovery paths.
- README and upgrade docs updated with examples showing both legacy token usage and rotating factory usage.
- package.json and CHANGELOG updated; version bumped to 3.1.0.

Example usage (from README):

const factory = new RotatingCredentialCache({
  refresh: async () => { /* call KMS / STS / tenant auth */ },
  leaseWindowMs: 10_000
});

for await (const msg of PullStreamIterable.connect({url, credentialFactory: factory})) {
  // consumer loop; safe to await inside
}

Backward compatibility and migration notes: The old SDK entrypoints that accept a static apiKey/token still work unchanged. The RotatingCredentialFactory is an opt-in argument to clients that construct streaming connections. The default reconnect behavior is slightly more conservative (longer initial backoff) to avoid aggressive reconnect loops during mass rotation events; this is configurable.

Security considerations: The rotating factory is designed to keep secrets out of long-lived closures and to surface an explicit refresh lifecycle. The default implementation retains a short in-memory lease but exposes a clear onChange hook so host processes can scrub state if necessary.

Performance: PullStreamIterable introduces a tiny allocation per iterator but amortizes reconnect cost across many messages. Benchmarks included in tests/bench show negligible per-message overhead (~0.3% median) for steady-state streaming.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice focused change. A couple of asks: 1) make the default RotatingCredentialCache leak-free when shutdown happens (unsubscribe handlers), 2) add a test for >1 concurrent iterator sharing the same credential factory. See inline comments.
Sofia Alvarez (author): Addressed both: cache now exposes shutdown() and iterators share the same event emitter under a WeakRef; added tests for concurrent iterators. PTAL.

Nora Kim: Please add a short note in migrations.md about backoff tuning for high-throughput customers (they hit reconnect storms on large fleet rotations). Also: confirm that the pullstream iterable won't reorder messages when reconnecting.

Sofia Alvarez (author): Added migration note and clarified guarantee: messages are yielded in server order per connection; reconnects start a fresh stream (server-supplied cursor required for in-order resume). Clarified in README.
Elias Zhang: CI flake on Node 14 matrix; test harness assumed global AbortController. Fixed polyfill usage and re-ran CI.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after small nitfix to JSDoc types.
